thread:
deploy-bot: publish job started for image `redwood/runtime:release-2026-03-15` (build 4821) -> FAILED in eu-west-1: provenance attestation digest mismatch and registry rejected due to tag immutability. logs:
```
ERROR: provenance check failed: expected sha256:4a7d... got sha256:9f2b...
Caused-by: cosign verification passed but manifest digest differs from pinned manifest
Registry response: 409 Tag immutability violation
```
Will retry per policy in 10m. cc @ian @maria @julie

ian: ack, looking. do we know which stage introduced the differing digest? mirror job? cosign key rotation? :thinking:

maria: seeing same. yesterday we rotated cosign key for eu registry at ~03:40 UTC then promoted signer. staging pushes looked fine. this smells like a mirror replication lag or an old manifest in regional mirror.

julie: deploybot log shows `Tag immutability violation` when trying to push same tag with new digest. so retagging same name won't work in prod because immutability policy is enabled.

ryan: if we can't overwrite the tag we have two options: 1) push new tag with new digest and update release metadata to pin to digest, or 2) abort and fallback to previously deployed digest (rollback). which is preferable?

ian: prefer push new tag then update release notes and canary routing to new digest, but that requires a change window because we would update release metadata for prod. outside window we mustn't change pinned deploy targets.

maria: does deploybot support promoting by digest right now? iirc there's a `--digest` flag to promote like `deploybot promote --image redwood/runtime@sha256:9f2b...`

julie: it does but our release policy forbids direct digest promotions outside the change window without SRE signoff. we should escalate to oncall if we think customer impact is high.

sre-oncall: oncall here. what's the rollback risk? if we leave current canary, traffic might hit older manifest with different layers. any breaking ABI concerns?

ian: runtime change is purely a packaging fix (missing metadata blob) so older digest is safe. no API changes. we can hold and let deploybot retry, but retries fail due to immutability. so automatic recover won't happen.

ryan: decision: put release on HOLD for prod. we will: (a) open a patch retag PR to push `release-2026-03-15-v2` -> sha256:9f2b..., (b) update release notes with digest pin and rollback instructions, (c) schedule manual promote in change window 2026-03-15 18:00-19:00 UTC with SRE present.

maria: I'll run the retag push to staging mirror now and pre-create the digest-tag mapping. command:
```
# push retag locally to eu mirror
docker pull redwood/runtime@sha256:9f2b...
docker tag redwood/runtime@sha256:9f2b... eu.gcr.io/redwood/runtime:release-2026-03-15-v2
docker push eu.gcr.io/redwood/runtime:release-2026-03-15-v2
```

julie: once that's up, i'll prepare the deploybot promote command and the release note patch. add note: customers using `:release-2026-03-15` should pin to digest for determinism.

sre-oncall: i'll standby for change window. if anyone escalates before window, page me. otherwise hold until 18:00 UTC.

deploy-bot: scheduled retry attempt #1 in 9m (automatic). manual promote blocked by immutability; awaiting manual `promote --digest` during change window.

ryan: also, add a postmortem flag on the release so research team can trace mirror/rotation interaction. tagging: `postmortem-required`.

ian: noted. will follow up with logs and the cosign rotation timeline in the PM doc. thanks all. :thumbsup:
